title: 3D-Carbon: An Analytical Carbon Modeling Tool for 3D and 2.5D Integrated Circuits
problem: There is a lack of carbon modeling tools for 3D/2.5D integrated circuits despite their increasing deployment. Current approaches do not quantify lifecycle carbon emissions (manufacturing and use phases) for these advanced integration technologies.
motivation: Environmental sustainability is critical across the IC lifecycle, and 3D/2.5D technologies are essential for meeting growing computational demands, making carbon footprint quantification vital.
method: 3D-Carbon analytically models lifecycle carbon emissions for 3D/2.5D ICs by accounting for both savings and overheads from advanced integration technologies. The tool incorporates practical deployment constraints like bandwidth and validates against established baselines through case studies in autonomous vehicle systems.
key_novelty: First analytical carbon lifecycle modeling framework designed specifically for 3D/2.5D integrated circuits that simultaneously accounts for integration technology benefits and overheads.
contributions: Analytical carbon modeling tool tailored for 3D/2.5D IC lifecycle assessment
Quantification of carbon emissions across manufacturing and operational phases
Integration of practical deployment constraints into carbon modeling
Validation methodology and case studies in autonomous vehicle domain
limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed; work positioned as foundational for future sustainable 3D/2.5D IC development.
primary_theme: Carbon footprint modeling for advanced IC packaging
